12 A bullet of mass 8.0 g travels at a speed of 300 m s–1. The bullet hits a target and stops after a
time of 100 µs.
What is the average force exerted by the target on the bullet?
A
24 N
B
240 N
C
2400 N
D
24 000 N

hints: Convert the given $8.0 \text{ g}$ to $\text{kg}$ and the stopping time $100 \text{ } \mu\text{s}$ to $\text{s}$ before any calculation.
Link the bullet stopping to momentum loss: initial momentum $p = mv$ falls to zero, so the target must supply impulse $F t = \Delta p$.
Calculate $p = 0.0080 \times 300$ in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$, then divide by $1.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ s}$ and check the power of 10 against the $24 \text{ N}$ to $24\,000 \text{ N}$ options.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: $m = 8.0 \text{ g}$, $v = 300 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ dropping to $0$, and stopping time $t = 100 \text{ } \mu\text{s}$.
Convert to SI units: $m = 8.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kg} = 0.0080 \text{ kg}$ and $t = 100 \times 10^{-6} \text{ s} = 1.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ s}$.
State the governing rule for average force: impulse equals change in momentum, $F t = \Delta p = mv - 0$, so $F = mv/t$.
Substitute with units: $F = (0.0080 \text{ kg})(300 \text{ m s}^{-1})/(1.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ s})$.
Work out the numerator: initial momentum $p = 2.4 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, so $F = 2.4 / 1.0 \times 10^{-4} = 2.4 \times 10^{4} \text{ N}$.
This is $24\,000 \text{ N}$ in the direction opposing motion. This is option D

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1000, from using mass as $8.0 \text{ g}$ instead of $0.0080 \text{ kg}$ in $F = mv/t$.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 100, from an error converting $100 \text{ } \mu\text{s}$ to seconds or missing a power of 10.

C.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10, from using $1000 \text{ } \mu\text{s} = 1 \text{ ms}$ instead of $100 \text{ } \mu\text{s} = 1.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ s}$.

D.explanation: Correct average force from $F = mv/t$ with SI units, giving $2.4 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ divided by $1.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ s}$.
